newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas urges resistance against Israeli settlement.
newsitem.headline: Hamas urges resistance against Israeli settlement.

text.p: The Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas called on Tuesday for a Palestinian uprising to protest the start of work at a planned Israeli settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"The Palestinian Authority should answer the call of the Palestinian people to go into continuous intifada (uprising)," Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghoshe said.
Israeli soldiers on Tuesday scuffled with Arabs near the planned Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, minutes after bulldozers broke ground on the housing project.

Ghoshe criticised Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat "for using only peaceful means" to protest the groundbreaking at Jabal Abu Ghneim, known as Har Homa in Israel, and for not cutting contact between Israel and Palestinians.
Suicide bombers from the military wing of Hamas, which rejects the Palestinian-Israeli self-rule deal as a sell-out, killed dozens of Israelis in a series of attacks a year ago.
"The road of resistance is the only road which can affect the Israelis," Ghoshe told Reuters. "Peaceful pressure...will not get anything from the Israelis."

Goshe said the new "intifada" should not be limited to a few days of conflict, like the fighting in September after Israel opened a tunnel by Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in that confrontation.
"The young people are eager to start the intifada and not stop until the occupation is ended," Ghoshe said.
He said the settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim "is not about a building on a mountain."
"It is the issue of Jerusalem and all Palestine," he said.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians say East Jerusalem, captured by Israeli forces during the 1967 Middle East war, will form the capital of their future state.
